_comment: Read by scripts/req-trace.ts. Two maps, both optional.
parts: requirement ID -> { part id -> what that part requires }. A requirement written as one sentence with
several obligations has no (a)/(b) enumerators for the tool to split on, so its parts are declared here.
A test then claims a part with `@verifies REQ-X-NN#a`; a part no test claims is reported as a gap.
Parts are the obligations of the requirement text and add no requirement of their own (CLAUDE.md §18).
nonTest: requirement ID -> { method, reason } for a requirement verified by inspection, analysis or
demonstration, so it is not reported as untested. Declare it only where the owning document says so.

REQ-UPG-01.a: A T1-identity unit never has a T2 stimulation enable granted (cervical VNS, clinical tACS / HD-tDCS, 1170 nm, TMS), refused in the partition that owns the enables
REQ-UPG-01.b: T2 software features unlock only against the signed tier identity, never against app UI state or the app-computed NP_PROTO_FLAG_T2_TIER
REQ-UPG-01.c: Fail closed: a missing or non-verifying identity is T1
REQ-UPG-01.d: The refusal is presented as F4, never as a missing module (F1)

REQ-UPG-02.a: The tier identity is written once, at manufacture, bound to the device and signed
REQ-UPG-02.b: No field path writes or changes it: not the app, OTA, a service partner, the depot or a purchase

REQ-UPG-03.a: The tile socket (mechanical, electrical, inventory and UID protocol) is kept compatible on every T2 configuration
REQ-UPG-03.b: The hub accessory ports used by A13, the audio cups and the intranasal probe are kept compatible
REQ-UPG-03.c: The lens mount is kept compatible
REQ-UPG-03.d: A change to one of these interfaces is made to both tiers or to neither

REQ-CVNS-09.a: Trigger: heart-rate change > 15 BPM within 5 s
REQ-CVNS-09.d: Enable GPIO low < 100 ms from detection
REQ-CVNS-09.f: App confirmation and repeat impedance before re-enable

REQ-CONSENT-13.a: After blanket withdrawal the device processes no study descriptor, whatever its issue date, categories or elements
REQ-CONSENT-13.b: After withdrawing from a study, that study is never processed again, whatever a re-issue says
REQ-CONSENT-13.c: No further extract is generated or transmitted for any data period, including sessions that predate the withdrawal (not built)
REQ-CONSENT-13.d: Results notifications for studies already joined continue and carry no new data (not built)

DI-SAFE-02.a: The safety MCU receives a heartbeat every 200 ms
DI-SAFE-02.b: A 1.5 s timeout without a heartbeat is a fault
DI-SAFE-02.c: On timeout all stimulation GPIO is cut off within 50 ms
DI-SAFE-02.d: The fault latch requires an explicit clear

REQ-FWHUB-18.a: The session signature goes in its own command frame, carrying the hash and the signature, and requests no enable (step 2 of §7.3)
REQ-FWHUB-18.b: No non-zero enable is requested before the next heartbeat reply shows SIG_PENDING cleared; a signature still pending aborts the session

DI-SAFE-11.a: Firmware build flag NP_MODE_F_REGULATORY_CLEARED = 0 until the RISK-03 Q-13 opinion is received, and Mode F emits nothing while it is 0
DI-SAFE-11.c: Mode F needs a separate explicit user consent, distinct from session consent
DI-SAFE-11.d: The right-temple amber LED shows a triple pulse (3 x 150 ms) while Mode F is active, and it is not suppressible

REQ-FWHUB-23.a: The cVNS PPG sample rate is pinned and compile-time asserted
REQ-FWHUB-23.b: The cardiac baseline is not waivable by a descriptor

SWR-HV-06.a: The hardware version is held in one place on the helmet and is always there: a consumer takes the helmet's value and keeps none of its own
SWR-HV-06.b: It is part of the tier identity, in the upper nibble of the tier byte, and is read by the safety MCU (from a record that verifies for this unit)
SWR-HV-06.c: It is given to the main processor over the SPI link
SWR-HV-06.e: Nothing in the field writes or changes it
SWR-HV-06.f: At most 16 hardware versions exist: a value outside the field's versions is not a version
SWR-HV-06.g: The factory step writes and verifies it, checking it against the board's revision before programming (not built)

SWR-HV-07.a: A unit with no readable version (no record, a malformed record, one that does not verify) reads as version 1 and is not faulted
SWR-HV-07.b: The default is removed in the same change that adds hardware version 2, and that removal is a checked item on the increment record (not due until version 2)

SWR-FM-02.a: A family has releases, and a release has one variant for each hardware version
SWR-FM-02.b: A release is a major.minor version of a predefined protocol
SWR-FM-02.c: A variant is the compiled content for one hardware version, with its own hash
SWR-FM-02.d: Retargeting a protocol to another hardware version adds a variant to the same family and does not start a new family
SWR-FM-02.e: Variants are independent after creation and linked only for lookup

SWR-SS-02.a: A session beyond a defined health-safety limit does not run without the user's explicit acknowledgement
SWR-SS-02.b: The acknowledgement is made in the path that signs the protocol, so the app's screen alone cannot skip it
SWR-SS-02.c: The request names the limit and the amount by which the session exceeds it

REQ-SHDR-04.a: The pinned set holds a primary and at least one backup key
REQ-SHDR-04.b: The app refuses a TLS handshake whose leaf SPKI SHA-256 is not in the pinned set
REQ-SHDR-04.c: The pinned hashes are production values, not placeholders

SWR-MG-11.calls: The common cloud storage API covers only what backup and restore need: put and get the encrypted bundle, find it, write a claim marker with create-if-absent, read the claim, write and read the confirmation, and release a claim
SWR-MG-11.verified: For each provider the conditional-write behaviour of the storage the app actually uses is verified against the provider's current documentation and recorded with the date
SWR-MG-11.contract: A contract test suite is run against each provider, including two simultaneous claim writes

REQ-FWHUB-64.a: the sockets the helmet version has, each of which a protocol must address validly, the count and the set of addresses defined per hardware version and read at runtime
REQ-FWHUB-64.b: how many of those sockets are filled, which is known at runtime
REQ-FWHUB-64.c: the power and heat limits in force at that moment, determined at runtime from the power sources and how they are being used
REQ-FWHUB-64.d: no count fixed at build time, and no array sized for a typical session, is a limit: capacity is the 7-bit address domain

REQ-SIMFW-01.reason: NP-SIM-FW-001 §5 names scripts/check-sim-host-only.ts, with a self-test over the bad trees, as the check that fails a device target linking the sim layer

REQ-NPPS-13.reason: NP-NPPS-REF-001 §14 names inspection of generated files as the verification

REQ-CONSENT-08.reason: docs/reference/consent-engine.md §6.4 names inspection of the S1 copy in locales/ as the verification

REQ-FWHUB-01.reason: NP-FW-HUB-001 §10.1 names scripts/check-hub-bringup-order.ts as the check

REQ-FWHUB-28.reason: NP-FW-HUB-001 §10.1 names scripts/check-hub-wire-format.ts, with 15 perturbation fixtures, as the check

REQ-FWHUB-30.reason: NP-FW-HUB-001 §10.1 says the task count is gated: counted, not read
